Blood glucose refers to the glucose present in the blood, which serves as the main energy source for the human body. It is produced from digested carbohydrates in food, breakdown of stored liver glycogen, and conversion of fats and proteins. The normal blood glucose range is 3.9–6.1 mmol/L.

Blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) is a core indicator for evaluating the oxygen delivery efficiency of human blood. It reflects the actual oxygen carrying level of the body by detecting the percentage of oxygenated hemoglobin combined with oxygen in the blood to the total amount of hemoglobin that can be combined. This value is an important reference for the function of the respiratory and circulatory systems. Healthy people in plain areas usually maintain a range of 95%-100%, but physiological fluctuations may occur due to individual physical differences, adaptability to the plateau environment, and chronic diseases. It should be noted that the data of daily monitoring equipment is only for health reference and has no clinical diagnostic value. If abnormal values ​​are found or there are health concerns, it is recommended to immediately seek professional medical advice from a practicing physician.

Blood pressure is composed of systolic and diastolic pressures and serves as a key indicator for assessing cardiovascular system function. The average systolic and diastolic pressures displayed in this app are calculated based on multiple measurements to reflect the overall blood pressure level over a certain period. According to common blood pressure classification standards, the app categorizes blood pressure status based on systolic and diastolic readings: - **Hypotension**: Systolic <90 mmHg or diastolic <60 mmHg - **Normal blood pressure**: Systolic 90–119 mmHg and diastolic 60–79 mmHg - **Elevated blood pressure**: Systolic 120–139 mmHg or diastolic 80–89 mmHg - **Stage 1 hypertension (mild)**: Systolic 140–159 mmHg or diastolic 90–99 mmHg - **Stage 2 hypertension (moderate)**: Systolic 160–179 mmHg or diastolic 100–109 mmHg - **Stage 3 hypertension (severe)**: Systolic ≥180 mmHg or diastolic ≥110 mmHg Additionally, when systolic ≥140 mmHg and diastolic <90 mmHg, isolated systolic hypertension may be indicated. Monitoring data may be influenced by factors such as measurement posture, emotional state, activity level, and individual differences. It is intended solely for health management reference and lacks clinical diagnostic significance. If blood pressure remains abnormal or symptoms like dizziness or palpitations occur, prompt consultation with a healthcare professional is recommended. Please note that this feature is not designed for medical purposes. If you have any health concerns, consult a qualified medical practitioner.

Heart rate variability (HRV) is used to measure the time between heartbeats. Heart rate variability contains information about the regulation of the cardiovascular system by neurohumoral factors, which can then be used to determine the status and prevention of cardiovascular diseases. This may also be a valuable indicator for predicting sudden cardiac death and arrhythmia. When you are under some kind of stress, your heart rate usually increases, and your heart rate variability decreases at this time. The lower the heart rate variability, the higher the stress.Less than 30 is low, 30--60 is normal, 61--101 is good, and greater than 101 is excellent.

This counter is specially designed for people of various religions. It is suitable for Buddhist chanting, Islamic prayer, Christian devotion, and more. It accurately records the number of prayers and supports custom cycle goals to fit different usage habits.

The core indicator of stress assessment is heart rate variability (HRV), which refers to the slight fluctuations between heartbeats. Under high stress, sympathetic nervous activity increases, leading to a decrease in HRV; conversely, under parasympathetic dominance, HRV increases. The device continuously collects heart rate data through PPG or ECG electrodes and calculates the stress index using time/frequency domain analysis (such as RMSSD, LF/HF ratio). A value less than 30 indicates relaxation, 30–60 is normal, 60–80 is moderate, and above 80 is high.

Body temperature data is only used as a reference for health values, please do not use it for medical purposes.

A person\'s normal body temperature varies depending on the part being measured. Cold drinks, hot drinks, strenuous exercise, bathing, etc. will all affect the measurement results. It is necessary to wait 30 minutes before taking another measurement. A person\'s body temperature will change a little during a day. For example, the body temperature in the afternoon will be slightly higher than the body temperature in the morning, but the fluctuation range will not exceed 1°C. The standard of normal body temperature is determined based on multiple values and is not absolute. For example, the basic metabolic rate of the elderly is low, and the body temperature can be slightly lower than this range. In children, the metabolism is fast, and the body temperature can be slightly elevated.
